constructivism: Knowledge is rebuilt as a mental model, not copied in. Reciting a fact while still feeling the wrong prediction is the tell.
assimilation: New experience is forced into the old model (trick, fluke, special case). The schema itself does not move.
accommodation: The mental model itself changes so experience can fit. Explaining the demo away is the other move.
disequilibrium: Mismatch between model and reality that drives learning. Visible failure of your own output is the classic push.
mko: A person or tool that can currently do what the learner cannot. Software hints count.
zpd: What you can do with help but not alone. Temporary scaffolds belong here and should fade.
kirschner-2006: Learning can be constructive while teaching still needs strong guidance for novices. Minimal guidance overloads beginners.
constructionism: Learn by making a real shareable artifact. Public make makes thinking visible.
constructivism-vs-constructionism: Inside rebuild (mental model) versus outside make (artifact that drives learning). Related, not synonyms.
instructionism: Improve learning mainly by improving how teachers explain. Better telling as the whole fix.
wide-walls: Many kinds of personally meaningful projects on one tool - not merely many ages or devices.
low-floor-high-ceiling: Easy for beginners to start and still deep for experts, on the same system.
four-ps: Projects, Passion, Peers, Play - creative-learning design checklist.
body-syntonic: Understand the program by acting the motion with your body first, then code it.
lecture: Word root is reading aloud. Historical teacher reading material to the class.
di-vs-discovery: False either-or. How expert the learner is should dial how much guidance you give.
faultless-communication: If they have not learned, the instruction has not taught. Fix materials before blaming the student.
di-vs-di: lowercase di = teacher-led teaching in general; DI = Engelmann and Becker's named scripted program.
gradual-release: I do, we do, you do - responsibility shifts from teacher to learner across three phases.
operant: Voluntary behavior shaped by what follows it. Consequences steer chosen acts.
classical: Pair stimuli until an automatic response transfers. Involuntary association, not chosen acts.
positive-reinforcement: Add something liked; behavior goes up.
negative-reinforcement: Remove something disliked; behavior goes up. Still reinforcement, not punishment.
positive-punishment: Add something disliked; behavior goes down.
negative-punishment: Remove something liked; behavior goes down.
reinforcement-vs-punishment: Reinforcement increases behavior; punishment decreases it. Positive=add, negative=remove. Sort up/down first.
cognitivism-displaced-behaviorism: Watching only outward acts could not explain abstraction, transfer, or novel solving. The mind had to come back into the story.
immediate-reinforcement: Consequence must land right after the behavior. Delayed feedback weakens the pairing.
ecological-cognition: Study thinking in messy everyday settings, not only clean labs.
newell-simon: Build an internal problem picture and search possible moves - problem-space search, not S-R alone.
cognitivist-feedback: Explain why the answer failed so the mental model updates. Bare wrong/try-again mostly nudges the next click.
cognitive-load: Intrinsic=content hardness; extraneous=junk design; germane=useful thinking. Cut clutter; sequence hard ideas.
image-principle: Adding a talking-head face to narration usually does not improve learning and can steal attention.
coherence-principle: Cute non-teaching visuals can hurt learning by wasting limited attention.
self-reflection: After performance, judge how it went and why. Part of self-regulated learning.
fluency-illusion: Ease of rereading feels like knowing but is not recall. Practice tests expose the gap.
monitoring-capacity: Stress can use up the attention needed to notice you are lost. Monitoring needs spare capacity.
guided-participation: Learn by joining real activity beside more experienced people - not only hearing a talk about it.
lpp: Newcomers do real low-stakes work at the edge of a community, then move toward the center.
cultural-variation: More than one valid way to reason or represent. Do not force a single style as the only correct one.
zpd-vs-scaffolding: ZPD is the zone (gap); scaffolding is temporary help inside that zone. Where versus what support.
mastery-oriented: Success means actually understanding, not looking better than others.
espn-top-10: Performance-approach hunts the highlight reel; performance-avoidance dodges the blooper reel - often on the same attempt.
belonging: Message that feeling out of place is normal and temporary can raise motivation and grades.
self-determination: Motivation needs autonomy, competence, and relatedness.
remote-proctoring: Systems struggled more with darker-skinned faces; captive users take uneven harm.
ai-feedback-demographics: Girls and underrepresented minorities got less critical feedback - softer is not equal help.
matthew-effect: Poorly designed EdTech helps the already-ahead first; the gap can widen early.
learning-styles: Matching teaching to VAK styles is a myth. Real differences: prior knowledge, language, access, disability.
assessment: Measure this student's learning for a grade or feedback - one person's reading.
evaluation: Use those measures to judge whether a tool or curriculum works - the design, not one grade alone.
